subject.title: fix(codex): reject hex/exponent computer wait duration strings

question: Should the Codex outer watchdog adopt this strict duration grammar before the computer-tool executor's own accepted-input contract is proven to match it?
rationale: This PR intentionally changes compatibility behavior at a timeout boundary, while the supplied proof exercises only the resolver and not the executor whose runtime the deadline must cover.

options.title: Align watchdog and executor
options.body: Verify the computer schema and execution parser, then share or parity-test one normalization rule so accepted durations always receive a sufficient outer deadline.

options.title: Accept watchdog narrowing
options.body: Land the resolver-only change after explicitly confirming that non-decimal string durations are unsupported and cannot execute longer downstream.

options.title: Preserve current coercion
options.body: Keep the shipped watchdog behavior until a separate owner-boundary change rejects or normalizes the same values during computer execution.

recommendation.title: Align watchdog and executor
recommendation.body: Verify the computer schema and execution parser, then share or parity-test one normalization rule so accepted durations always receive a sufficient outer deadline.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available routing signal is recent work on the surrounding Codex runtime and projection behavior.
